text: Rodong Newspaper Rodong Newspaper Rodong Newspaper Thursday, April 9, 2026, page 5 [There is a photo] Salt production remains from the Bronze Age and Neolithic Age have been newly discovered in the Woneup-ro-dong area of Oncheon-gun, Nampo-si. Salt production remains from the Bronze Age and the Neolithic Age have been discovered in the Won-eup-ro-dong area of Oncheon-gun, Nampo-si.

In keeping with the Party's will to enrich the treasure trove of cultural heritage by excavating more historical relics created by our people, the research group of the Archeology Research Institute of the Academy of Social Sciences has deepened the investigation and excavation of historical relics.

In this process, the Bronze Age and the Neolithic Age were discovered for the first time in our country in the Woneup-ro-dong area of Oncheon-gun, Nampo-si.(５ ０００~５ ５００years ago)A salt water storage facility and a salt roasting facility, which are relics of salt production, were discovered.
The salt water storage facility is hemispherical in shape, which is advantageous for storing salt water, and has two cultural layers.(Stratum containing archaeological remains)It is separated by

In the Ut culture layer, hardened gamtang layers used to store salt water and fragments of top bowls from the Bronze Age are found., In the lower cultural layer, a thick layer of mud mixed with wood ash that was spread to store salt water and fragments of carved vessels from the Neolithic Age appeared.
The salt grilling facility also has two cultural layers.

In the upper cultural layer, there are fire pit facilities with a history of concentrating salt water and fragments of top bowls from the Bronze Age., In the lower cultural layer, undated fire pit facilities and fragments of engraved vessels from the Neolithic Age were unearthed.

In the process of comparing and analyzing the composition and salinity of the soil of the salt water storage facility and the surrounding soil by applying various analysis methods in connection with the relevant units, the research group concluded that the soil salinity of the salt water storage facility was much higher than the salinity of the surrounding soil and that this relic was a salt-producing relic.

In addition, by measuring the age of the earthenware vessels, the earthenware vessels excavated from the Ut culture layer date back to the Bronze Age, 5000 years ago., It has been scientifically explained that the earthenware vessels excavated from the lower cultural layer belong to the Neolithic Age, 5500 years ago.

According to the Archaeological Society of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea, the artifacts and earthenware vessels excavated from the Wonup-rodongjagu area of Oncheon-gun, Nampo-si, After reviewing the analysis data on the soil, the upper cultural layer was discovered in the Bronze Age 5000 years ago., It was confirmed that the lower cultural layer is the remains of our ancestors producing salt by boiling down sea water during the Neolithic Age 5500 years ago.

In addition, it was evaluated that this historical relic has national treasure value, showing the excellence of our wise and civilized people as clear evidence proving that the Taedonggangryu Station area, centered on Pyongyang, is one of the birthplaces of human culture.
